target_customer: Low-income parents and caregivers of children aged 0 to 6 in India, reached directly and through state governments and anganwadi workers; funded by philanthropy and government partnerships
problem: Parents with low literacy in low-resource settings lack guidance on early childhood development, the period when most brain development happens.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by grants and prizes, delivering audio phonecasts and WhatsApp content, scaled via state government partnerships
product_category: Edtech nonprofit, parent education for early childhood

founders.name: Sneha Sheth
prior_employers: Advisory work for Goldman Sachs, Gates Foundation, Teach For India, UN Women, per YC bio
education: MBA, UC Berkeley (YC bio says she started Dost while completing it)
founders.background_notes: Mulago Rainer Arnhold Fellow and GLG Social Impact Fellow per the YC page. Current CEO is Richa Shukla per the Dost site.

founders.name: Sindhuja Jeyabal
education: Master's, UC Berkeley, technology for international development
founders.background_notes: From the YC page. Search results describe her as co-founder and CTO.

competitors.name: Read to Kids (Worldreader)
competitors.what: Mobile reading program for parents and children in India, run with Results for Development and Pearson
competitors.traction_then: India pilot ran 2015 to 2017 and won a 2017 mBillionth Award in the learning category

technical_complexity.rationale: Automated voice calls and content delivery that works on basic phones, plus WhatsApp content. The hard part was behavior design and distribution rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Government partnerships and content in local languages give some position, but the model can be copied and as a nonprofit it has no pricing moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; Dost instead works inside the public anganwadi system and with state governments.

market_need_then: The Dost site and YC page cite 150 million under-resourced caregivers in India and that 90 percent of brain development happens early. A 2018 YourStory profile reported growth from 300 users in February 2017 to over 10,000 in under a year.

branding.name_origin: Dost means friend in Hindi, per the Dost site; a founder framed the idea as being a friend to parents

identity.mascot_or_character: Arushi, the friendly named voice of the Dost calls, per a partner profile
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, fun and empathetic, framed as a friend to parents

branding.brand_signature: Arushi, the voice of Dost phonecasts

brand_strength.rationale: The name and the Arushi voice match the friend positioning and are sourced, but no press about the brand itself beyond impact profiles was found.

outcome_analysis: Dost is a nonprofit that grew from a pilot with a few hundred mothers to reaching over 100,000 families by working with state governments. It won small prizes and grants such as the Next Billion Edtech Prize and MIT Solve, and remains active with a new CEO. Distribution through the public anganwadi system is its main advantage; funding is philanthropic and hard to total from public sources.
notes: Funding is philanthropic and incomplete. Other grants appear only in search snippets and are not recorded as rounds: MIT Solve $10,000 (2019), Morgridge Family Foundation $10,000 (2020), a $174,288 FFWD grant (Cause IQ). CB Insights reports $260K total. YC page lists Mulago as a funder. Founding year conflicts: YC says 2017, some sources say 2016 or 2018. The Next Billion prize amount comes from a Hans India snippet, not opened. Search for later news returned unrelated U.S. Education Department stories.
